items_list.fact: Diffusion models (Sohl-Dickstein 2015) elegant but had never produced competitive samples
items_list.where: The paper tab, Problem
checks: there has been no demonstration that they are capable of generating high quality samples

items_list.fact: GANs dominated sample quality but trained unstably and lacked likelihoods
items_list.where: The paper tab, Problem (sourced to Table 1 and the ADA abstract)
checks: GANs had the best samples but no likelihood

items_list.fact: Autoregressive models and flows had likelihoods but weaker samples
items_list.where: The paper tab, Problem (Table 1 numbers)
checks: Autoregressive models and flows had likelihoods but weaker samples

items_list.fact: The open question: can a diffusion model trained with plain VI generate high quality images, and what parameterisation makes it work?
items_list.where: The paper tab, Problem
checks: can a diffusion model, trained with plain variational inference, actually generate high-quality images, and what parameterisation makes that work?

items_list.fact: Forward process: fixed, parameter-free Markov chain, T = 1000, linear beta 1e-4 to 0.02
items_list.where: The paper tab, Forward process
checks: The forward or diffusion process is a fixed Markov chain

items_list.fact: q(x_t | x_{t-1}) = N(sqrt(1 - beta_t) x_{t-1}, beta_t I)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Forward process, Eq. 2

items_list.fact: alpha_t, alpha-bar_t; q(x_t | x_0) closed form; x_t = sqrt(abar) x_0 + sqrt(1 - abar) eps
items_list.where: The paper tab, Forward process, Eq. 4; the animation and the t slider
checks: the chain collapses to a closed form, so any timestep can be reached in one jump

items_list.fact: Makes training cheap: random t, noise x_0 in one shot, no chain simulation
items_list.where: The paper tab, Forward process
checks: Training is therefore cheap: pick a random t and noise x 0 in one shot

items_list.fact: Schedule chosen so alpha-bar_T ~ 0, x_T ~ N(0, I)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Forward process; recomputed L_T

items_list.fact: Reverse process: learned chain from p(x_T) = N(0, I); p_theta(x_{t-1}|x_t) = N(mu_theta, sigma_t^2 I)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Reverse process, Eq. 1
checks: The reverse process is a Markov chain with learned Gaussian transitions

items_list.fact: Gaussian transitions right because for small beta the true reversal is approximately Gaussian
items_list.where: The paper tab, Idea
checks: When each forward step is small, its true reversal is close to Gaussian

items_list.fact: Reverse variances fixed (beta_t or beta-tilde_t, both work); only the mean learned
items_list.where: The paper tab, Reverse process

items_list.fact: ELBO decomposes into L_T + sum L_{t-1} + L_0 with L_{t-1} = KL(q(x_{t-1}|x_t,x_0) || p_theta)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Reverse process, Eq. 5

items_list.fact: Forward posterior Gaussian with known mean mu-tilde; KLs closed form, low variance, no Monte Carlo
items_list.where: The paper tab, Reverse process, Eq. 6 and 7

items_list.fact: L_T constant (forward fixed); L_0 discretised Gaussian decoder gives exact discrete likelihoods
items_list.where: The paper tab, Forward process (L_T), Training (decoder, Eq. 13)
checks: so the bound is a lossless codelength

items_list.fact: Key move: reparameterise; network predicts eps; mu_theta = (1/sqrt(alpha_t))(x_t - beta_t/sqrt(1-abar_t) eps_theta)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Predict the noise, Eq. 11
checks: a network ε θ predicts it

items_list.fact: Each L_{t-1} becomes a weighted MSE between eps and eps_theta
items_list.where: The paper tab, Predict the noise, Eq. 12
checks: Then each term of the bound is a weighted MSE on the noise

items_list.fact: L_simple = E ||eps - eps_theta(...)||^2, t ~ Uniform(1..T)
items_list.where: The paper tab, L_simple, Eq. 14

items_list.fact: Reweighting down-weights small-t terms, focuses on large-t (hard denoising); the ablation shows this is what sample quality needs
items_list.where: The paper tab, L_simple predict question and its weight chart
checks: down-weight[s] loss terms corresponding to small t
focus on more difficult denoising tasks at larger t
The ablation below shows this reweighting is exactly what sample quality needs

items_list.fact: Training: sample x_0, t, eps; one forward pass; MSE; SGD step
items_list.where: The paper tab, Training and sampling (Algorithm 1)
checks: Training is one forward pass and one MSE per example

items_list.fact: eps_theta is up to scale the score: grad log q(x_t|x_0) = -eps/sqrt(1-abar_t)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Predict the noise (marked as a derivation); Sample tab score field
checks: so ε θ is a scaled score estimate

items_list.fact: L_simple is denoising score matching over multiple noise scales (NCSN)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Predict the noise
checks: resembles denoising score matching over multiple noise scales

items_list.fact: Ancestral sampler x_{t-1} = ... + sigma_t z resembles annealed Langevin dynamics, eps_theta a learned gradient of the data density
items_list.where: The paper tab, Predict the noise; Algorithm 2
checks: resembles Langevin dynamics with ε θ as a learned gradient of the data density

items_list.fact: Equivalence (VI on a diffusion chain = DSM + Langevin) is the stated core contribution with the samples
items_list.where: The paper tab, Idea and Predict the noise
checks: denoising score matching here is variational inference on a sampling chain

items_list.fact: Architecture: U-Net (PixelCNN++ style), group norm, self-attention at 16x16, t via Transformer sinusoidal embeddings, weights shared across time
items_list.where: The paper tab, Training (details block); Then and now card
checks: a U-Net like an unmasked PixelCNN++

items_list.fact: CIFAR-10 unconditional FID 3.17 (SOTA at publication, beating most class-conditional models), IS 9.46
items_list.where: The paper tab, headline card and Results; Tables tab

items_list.fact: NLL <= 3.70 bits/dim (corrected: 3.70 is the true-bound model; the FID 3.17 model has 3.75)
items_list.where: The paper tab, Results (both values, with which model each belongs to)

the model trained on the true bound gets the better ≤ 3.70 (3.69) but an FID of only 13.51

items_list.fact: LSUN 256: Church FID 7.89, Bedroom FID 4.90, comparable to ProgressiveGAN; CelebA-HQ 256 samples
items_list.where: The paper tab, Results; Tables tab (Bedroom 4.90 is the larger model, 6.36 the standard one)

items_list.fact: Ablation Table 2: eps + fixed variances + L_simple wins; mu-tilde works only on the true ELBO; learned diagonal variances destabilise
items_list.where: The paper tab, Ablation (table, predict question, toy reproduction); Tables tab
checks: μ̃ works only on the true bound

items_list.fact: Rate-distortion: over half the codelength describes imperceptible detail; sampling as progressive decoding, coarse first
items_list.where: The paper tab, Progressive coding; Figure 5 rebuilt from Table 4

large-scale features appear first and details last

items_list.fact: Generalised bit-ordering view of autoregressive decoding
items_list.where: The paper tab, Progressive coding (details block)

items_list.fact: Caveats: likelihoods not competitive with strong AR models; sampling needs T = 1000 sequential evaluations
